works.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastic (PSNP) contaminants are widespread in the environment with potential adverse effects on male reproductive health. This study investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying PSNP-induced testicular dysfunction in rats and evaluated the protective effects of pirfenidone (PF) and tirzepatide (TZP). Twenty-four adult albino rats were included in the study. Eighteen rats received PSNP (1.5 mg/kg/day, orally) for 8 weeks, while six age-matched rats receiving deionized water by oral gavage served as negative controls. Beginning in week 5, PSNP-exposed rats were assigned to three groups (n = 6/group): vehicle-treated PSNP, PSNP+PF (100 mg/kg/day, orally), and PSNP+TZP (0.5 mg/kg/week, subcutaneously), with treatments continued for 4 weeks. PSNP exposure impaired testicular architecture, disrupted the blood–testis barrier, compromised steroidogenesis, and promoted testicular fibrosis. It also induced oxidative stress through dysregulation of the TXNIP/TRX system and enhanced pyroptosis, potentially through activation of the HMGB1/TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling pathway. Treatment with either PF or TZP markedly attenuated PSNP-induced alterations, preserved blood–testis barrier integrity, improved steroidogenic function, and reduced fibrosis, oxidative stress, and pyroptosis. These protective effects were associated with modulation of the TXNIP/TRX system and suppression of HMGB1/TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3-mediated pyroptotic signaling. Collectively, these findings identify PF and TZP as promising preclinical candidates for mitigating PSNP-induced testicular toxicity. Further mechanistic and translational studies are warranted to validate their potential role in protecting male reproductive health.
works.title: Tirzepatide Attenuates Polystyrene Nanoplastic-Induced Testicular Injury by Preserving the Blood–Testis Barrier and Suppressing Pyroptosis in Rats
